name: Functional Progress Model v1
purpose: Translate Can-Do evidence into an interpretable functional progress profile without reducing English ability to a single score.
principles: Communication is primary; grammar, vocabulary and pronunciation support communication.
Knowledge, ability and confidence are separate dimensions.
A learner can be progressing in one skill while remaining weak in another.
Mastery requires repeated successful evidence, not one successful attempt.
Failure routes the learner to a specific gap or prerequisite.
The model estimates functional CEFR-aligned progress; it does not certify CEFR.

evidenceLevels.description: Learner attempts the Can-Do; evidence may be incomplete.
Learner succeeds with meaningful prompts, models or scaffolding.
Learner succeeds independently on a familiar task.
Learner succeeds independently on repeated tasks with different content.
Learner uses the ability in a new but related context with limited preparation.

scoring.note: Dimension scores are normalized evidence measures, not percentages of English knowledge.
scoring.rule: Use domain-level profiles for decisions; the overall index is secondary and never replaces individual skill status.

canDoStatus.emerging: Attempted or partially successful; requires substantial support.
canDoStatus.developing: Can complete the task with some support or inconsistent performance.
canDoStatus.functional: Can complete the task independently on familiar content.
canDoStatus.consolidated: Can complete the task independently and consistently across varied familiar content.
canDoStatus.transferred: Can use the ability successfully in a new related context.

mastery.rule: A Can-Do should not become mastered from a single high score. Repeated independent evidence is required.
mastery.resourceRule: Grammar and vocabulary mastery is demonstrated through use in meaningful production, not isolated recognition alone.

gapDetection.rule: Prefer the smallest actionable gap that explains the failed Can-Do.
gapDetection.example: If a learner cannot explain a project because key vocabulary is missing, target vocabulary before assigning a broad grammar lesson.

confidence.role: Transversal diagnostic and progression indicator; confidence never substitutes for performance evidence.

interpretation.2: Could do it with a lot of help.
interpretation.3: Could do it with some help.

review.trigger: Review after success, repeated failure, or observed forgetting.
review.rule: Spacing applies to Can-Dos and language resources according to evidence, not simply to lesson completion.

personalization.principle: Prioritize high-value Can-Dos connected to the learner's real life, work and goals.
personalization.fallback: Use general familiar-life contexts when professional context is not relevant.

progression.A2: bilingual-by-default; build reliable everyday communication and basic interaction.
progression.A2Plus: English-first with Spanish support; connect ideas, experiences, work, opinions and short interactions.
progression.B1: English-first; handle familiar personal/professional communication with increasing independence and connected speech/writing.
progression.promotionRule: Do not promote by completing a fixed lesson count. Promotion depends on the relevant Can-Do evidence profile.
